original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-de-rham-affine}
Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of affine schemes given by the ring map
$R \to A$. Then $R\Gamma(X, \Omega^\bullet_{X/S}) = \Omega^\bullet_{A/R}$
in $D(R)$ and $H^i_{dR}(X/S) = H^i(\Omega^\bullet_{A/R})$.
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a ring homomorphism, $S=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, and $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. Write $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ for the relative de Rham complex of sheaves and $\Omega^\bullet_{A/R}$ for the algebraic de Rham complex of $A$ over $R$ (with $\Omega^p_{A/R}=\bigwedge_A^p\Omega^1_{A/R}$ and the exterior derivative). Then the canonical comparison map is an isomorphism
$$R\Gamma(X,\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})\simeq\Omega^\bullet_{A/R}\quad\text{in }D(R).$$
Consequently, for every integer $i$, $H^i_{dR}(X/S):=H^i(R\Gamma(X,\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}))\cong H^i(\Omega^\bullet_{A/R})$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-coherence-relative}
Let $p : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $p$ is quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, then $Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ is an object
of $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_S)$.
statement: Let $p:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes. Write $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}=(\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{d}\Omega^1_{X/S}\xrightarrow{d}\Omega^2_{X/S}\to\cdots)$ for the relative de Rham complex, where $\Omega^i_{X/S}=\bigwedge^i_{\mathcal O_X}\Omega^1_{X/S}$. Then the derived direct image $Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ belongs to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_S)$: every cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^n(Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})$ is quasi-coherent on $S$.
standalone_statement_draft: Let $p:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes. Write $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}=(\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{d}\Omega^1_{X/S}\xrightarrow{d}\Omega^2_{X/S}\to\cdots)$ for the relative de Rham complex, where $\Omega^i_{X/S}=\bigwedge^i_{\mathcal O_X}\Omega^1_{X/S}$. Then the derived direct image $Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ belongs to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_S)$: every cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^n(Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})$ is quasi-coherent on $S$.
hypotheses: $p:X\to S$ is a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes.
conclusions: For all $n\in\mathbb Z$, $\mathcal H^n(Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})$ is quasi-coherent.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-coherence-relative}
Let $p : X \to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes with $S$ locally
Noetherian. Then $Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ is an object
of $D_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_S)$.
statement: Let $p:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes, and assume $S$ is locally Noetherian. Let $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ denote the relative de Rham complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, with $\Omega^a_{X/S}=\bigwedge^a_{\mathcal O_X}\Omega^1_{X/S}$ placed in cohomological degree $a$. Then the derived direct image $Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ is an object of $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_S)$: its cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^n(Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})$ are coherent $\mathcal O_S$-modules for all integers $n$.

Let $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ denote the relative de Rham complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, with $\Omega^a_{X/S}=\bigwedge^a_{\mathcal O_X}\Omega^1_{X/S}$ placed in cohomological degree $a$. Then the derived direct image $Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ is an object of $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_S)$: its cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^n(Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})$ are coherent $\mathcal O_S$-modules for all integers $n$.
hypotheses: $p:X\to S$ is proper and $S$ is locally Noetherian.
conclusions: Every cohomology sheaf of $Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ is coherent on $S$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proper-smooth-de-Rham}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a proper smooth morphism of schemes. Then
$Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S}$, $p \geq 0$ and $Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ are
perfect objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_S)$ whose formation commutes
with arbitrary change of base.
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper, smooth morphism of schemes. For $p\geq 0$ put $\Omega^p_{X/S}=\bigwedge^p_{\mathcal O_X}\Omega^1_{X/S}$, and let $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ be the relative de Rham complex. Each $Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S}$ and the derived direct image $Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ are perfect objects of $D(\mathcal O_S)$.

More precisely, for every morphism $g:S'\to S$ of schemes, let $X'=X\times_S S'$, $g':X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to S'$ be the induced maps. For each $p\geq0$ the canonical derived base-change map
$$Lg^*(Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S})\longrightarrow Rf'_*\Omega^p_{X'/S'}$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_{S'})$, and so is the analogous map
$$Lg^*(Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})\longrightarrow Rf'_*\Omega^\bullet_{X'/S'}.$$

Each $Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S}$ and the derived direct image $Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ are perfect objects of $D(\mathcal O_S)$.

More precisely, for every morphism $g:S'\to S$ of schemes, let $X'=X\times_S S'$, $g':X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to S'$ be the induced maps. For each $p\geq0$ the canonical derived base-change map
$$Lg^*(Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S})\longrightarrow Rf'_*\Omega^p_{X'/S'}$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_{S'})$, and so is the analogous map
$$Lg^*(Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})\longrightarrow Rf'_*\Omega^\bullet_{X'/S'}.$$

conclusions: The derived pushforwards of every $\Omega^p_{X/S}$ and of the full relative de Rham complex are perfect and satisfy derived base change for every $S'\to S$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cup-product-graded-commutative}
Let $p : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The cup product on $H^*_{dR}(X/S)$ is associative and
graded commutative.
statement:
Let $p:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $H^i_{dR}(X/S)=\mathbb H^i(X,\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})$ its relative de Rham hypercohomology. Wedge multiplication of relative differential forms induces the de Rham cup product
$$\cup:H^i_{dR}(X/S)\times H^j_{dR}(X/S)\to H^{i+j}_{dR}(X/S).$$
This product is associative and graded commutative: for homogeneous classes $\alpha\in H^i_{dR}(X/S)$ and $\beta\in H^j_{dR}(X/S)$,
$$(\alpha\cup\beta)\cup\gamma=\alpha\cup(\beta\cup\gamma),\qquad \alpha\cup\beta=(-1)^{ij}\beta\cup\alpha.$$

$$\cup:H^i_{dR}(X/S)\times H^j_{dR}(X/S)\to H^{i+j}_{dR}(X/S).$$
This product is associative and graded commutative: for homogeneous classes $\alpha\in H^i_{dR}(X/S)$ and $\beta\in H^j_{dR}(X/S)$,
$$(\alpha\cup\beta)\cup\gamma=\alpha\cup(\beta\cup\gamma),\qquad \alpha\cup\beta=(-1)^{ij}\beta\cup\alpha.$$
hypotheses: $p:X\to S$ is a morphism of schemes.
conclusions: The cup product on the graded relative de Rham cohomology ring is associative and satisfies the Koszul sign rule.

statement:
Let $p:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, and define the total-degree-graded Hodge cohomology groups by
$$H^n_{\mathrm{Hodge}}(X/S)=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}H^b(X,\Omega^a_{X/S}).$$
Wedge multiplication of relative differential forms and cup multiplication in sheaf cohomology induce a product
$$\cup:H^i_{\mathrm{Hodge}}(X/S)\times H^j_{\mathrm{Hodge}}(X/S)\to H^{i+j}_{\mathrm{Hodge}}(X/S).$$
This product is associative and graded commutative with respect to the total degrees: for homogeneous $\alpha$ of total degree $i$ and $\beta$ of total degree $j$, $\alpha\cup\beta=(-1)^{ij}\beta\cup\alpha$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-kunneth-de-rham}
Assume $X$ and $Y$ are smooth, quasi-compact, with affine diagonal over
$S = \Spec(A)$. Then the map
$$
R\Gamma(X, \Omega^\bullet_{X/S})
\otimes_A^\mathbf{L}
R\Gamma(Y, \Omega^\bullet_{Y/S})
\longrightarrow
R\Gamma(X \times_S Y, \Omega^\bullet_{X \times_S Y/S})
$$
is an isomorphism in $D(A)$.
statement:
Let $A$ be a ring and $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. Let $a:X\to S$ and $b:Y\to S$ be smooth, quasi-compact morphisms of schemes whose diagonal morphisms $X\to X\times_S X$ and $Y\to Y\times_S Y$ are affine. Let $p:X\times_S Y\to X$ and $q:X\times_S Y\to Y$ be the projections. The external de Rham cup product, formed by pullback along $p,q$ and wedge multiplication, induces a canonical isomorphism
$$R\Gamma(X,\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R\Gamma(Y,\Omega^\bullet_{Y/S})\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\Gamma(X\times_S Y,\Omega^\bullet_{X\times_S Y/S})$$
in the derived category $D(A)$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-spectral-sequence-smooth}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and smooth
morphism of schemes over a base scheme $S$. There is a bounded spectral
sequence with first page
$$
E_1^{p, q} =
H^q(\Omega^p_{Y/S} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y}^\mathbf{L} Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/Y})
$$
converging to $R^{p + q}f_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$.
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes with $f$ smooth, quasi-compact, and quasi-separated. The differential sequence
$$0\to f^*\Omega^1_{Y/S}\to\Omega^1_{X/S}\to\Omega^1_{X/Y}\to0$$
is locally split and induces the filtration of $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ by exterior powers of $f^*\Omega^1_{Y/S}$, with
$$\operatorname{gr}^p_F\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}\cong f^{-1}\Omega^p_{Y/S}[-p]\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}\Omega^\bullet_{X/Y}.$$
The source asserts a bounded spectral sequence with $E_1^{p,q}=\mathcal H^q(\Omega^p_{Y/S}\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}^{\mathbf L}Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/Y})$ abutting to $\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})$.

Further work needed before promotion: check what "bounded" means in the source's unrestricted $Y\to S$ setting and whether a finiteness assumption is required. For example, when $f=\operatorname{id}_Y$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbf Q[x_1,x_2,\ldots])$ over $S=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbf Q)$, the potentially nonzero rows indexed by exterior degree $p$ are unbounded. Do not treat this draft as a validated theorem.
